tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

1	---
2	name: decode-at-depth-after-p15
3	description: "Decode rates against context depth after P15 (2026-09-22), the four terms a deep decode step is made of, and the three control knobs — supersedes the P10 table for decode."
4	metadata: 
5	  node_type: memory
6	  type: project
7	  originSessionId: dedbcc64-a855-44f2-a0fa-3d37d0946061
8	  modified: 2026-09-22T15:25:15.756Z
9	---
10	
11	**Quote this table for decode, not P10's and not P14's.** 48 layers, shipped
12	banks, `-pp 2048 -tg 16 -ctx 139000`, `wiki.test.raw`, write-up
13	`research/p15-decode-at-depth.md`.
14	
15	| depth | pp tok/s | tg tok/s | tg ms/tok |
16	|------:|---------:|---------:|----------:|
17	| 0 | 1150.7 | 29.73 | 33.6 |
18	| 8 000 | 969.6 | 28.78 | 34.8 |
19	| 32 000 | 915.3 | 28.72 | 34.8 |
20	| 64 000 | 892.8 | 28.14 | 35.5 |
21	| 128 000 | 829.4 | **27.20** | 36.8 |
22	| falloff | 0.72x | **0.91x** | |
23	
24	Decode at 128k was 22.58 before P15 and the falloff 0.76x. **Prefill did not
25	move** (826.5 → 829.4 at 128k) and is P14's; it was P15's control.
26	
27	**A deep decode step is four terms and nothing else.** Every other kernel in
28	the model is flat in depth — `moe.up` 5.44 ms a token at both ends, `dn.qkv`
29	4.39, `hc.cn` 2.33. At 128 000 cells, base → final:
30	
31	- `attn.attn.split` 4.109 → **1.571** (the gather+split, P15-3)
32	- host `gather`, i.e. `PLERows` 5.175 → **1.263** (P15-1)
33	- `attn.score` 2.533 → **0.995** (the stripe at 64, P15-2)
34	- `attn.select` 0.862 → **0.862** — untouched, and now the largest
35	  depth-scaling term left on the device
36	
37	**The largest one was on the host.** `PLERows(cfg, g.ids)` hashed the whole
38	sequence every token and sliced off the tail — 8.2 MB allocated and 2.05 M rows
39	per step at 128k to use sixteen. `PLERowsFrom` is the tail-only form and is
40	exact by construction. The `-depth` bench had been printing that as a `gather`
41	line growing 3.1% → 11.7% with depth for as long as it has existed. **Read the
42	host lines of the profile, not only the kernel ones.**
43	
44	**The control knobs**, all env, all on `cmd/llm -depth`:
45	
46	    LLM_ATTN_GATHER=0            # P8's block split, which is what decode had
47	    LLM_ATTN_GATHER_MIN=<cells>  # the depth the gathered arm turns on at
48	    LLM_ATTN_CELL_SPLITS=16      # P9's stripe count, shipped at 64
49	    LLM_ARENA_UNCACHED=1         # the arena memory type
50	    LLM_NO_PRERECORD=1           # re-record every decode step
51	
52	**The gates after touching any of this** (plus P7-P10's, in
53	[[context-depth-rates]]):
54	
55	    go test ./llm/ -run TestPLERowsFromIsTheTail                   # exact
56	    go test ./llm/ -run TestAttnGPUGatherSplitIsTheGather          # tolerance
57	    go test ./llm/ -run TestPrerecordedDecodeCrossesTheGatherBound # the epoch
58	
59	**Two traps this pass walked into, both worth remembering.** A split-kernel
60	test that uploads the whole fixture at once passes with 0.000e+00 on every arm,
61	because `attnSplits` refuses any batch wider than `attnSplitMaxRows` — a split
62	that never engaged looks exactly like a perfect one, so assert on a zero. And
63	the obvious test for the prerecord epoch — diff the logits across the bound
64	with the replay on and off — **cannot fail**, because below the selection's
65	2051-cell width the gathered and block kernels are bit-identical; assert the
66	mechanism (`preEpoch` against the depth) instead.
67	
68	**How to apply:** needs `LLM_BANK_CACHE` — see [[llm-bench-needs-bank-cache]],
69	[[strix-halo-bench-runs]], [[never-edit-source-during-a-sweep]] and
70	[[llm-resident-run]]. The fast loop is `-depths 128000 -pp 2048 -tg 8 -layers 4`,
71	~60 s an arm, and it reproduces the `attn.attn` ratios to the microsecond.
72	---
73	name: long-context-prefill-128k
74	description: "Prefill against depth out to 128k after P14 (2026-09-22): 826 tok/s at ubatch 2048 and 946 at 8192, the four changes, the four measured refusals, and the fast 4-layer probe."
75	metadata: 
76	  node_type: memory
77	  type: project
78	  originSessionId: 80f71c47-a621-4724-a77a-e285f8d84b61
79	  modified: 2026-09-22T11:38:44.739Z
80	---
81	
82	**128 000 cells prefills at 826.0 tok/s at ubatch 2048 and 946.1 at
83	8192 — `GOALS.md`'s 900 is met.** P13 left it at 563.6. 48 layers, shipped banks,
84	`wiki.test.raw`, one sequence walked forward, `-tg 8 -ctx 139000`. Write-up
85	`research/p14-prefill-at-depth.md`.
86	
87	| depth | P13 pp | P14 pp | | decode |
88	|------:|-------:|-------:|----:|-------:|
89	| 0 | 1129.3 | 1154.2 | 1.02x | 29.31 |
90	| 32 000 | 825.8 | 915.6 | 1.11x | 25.80 |
91	| 64 000 | 719.6 | 892.1 | 1.24x | 24.46 |
92	| 96 000 | 607.9 | 832.3 | 1.37x | 22.80 |
93	| **128 000** | **563.6** | **826.0** | **1.47x** | 22.18 |
94	
95	Falloff from depth zero **0.50x → 0.72x**. Against the ubatch at 128 000 alone
96	(two runs each): 826.0 at 2048, 886.1 at 4096 (the shipped
97	`-llm-batch`), **946.1 at 8192** — P12's trade at depth, so 8192 is a
98	batch summariser's setting. **Decode is the control and did not move.**
99	
100	**Four changes.**
101	
102	1. **The selection runs over block scores, not the expanded per-cell tensor**
103	   (`llm_attn_selblk.comp`). All `ratio` cells of a pooled block carry one score,
104	   so a weighted select over `nKV/ratio` entries is the same threshold, ties and
105	   bitmask. `attn.select` 0.281 → **0.020** (13.8x), `attn.expand` deleted, and
106	   **1.14 GB of arena** freed at ubatch 2048. Bit-identical, gated by
107	   `TestAttnGPUSelectBlocksIsTheCellSelect` over four chunk schedules.
108	2. **The attention runs over a per-cell gather** (`llm_attn_gather.comp` +
109	   `llm_attn_wmma.comp -DGATHER`). Per query tile, the union of its rows'
110	   selections compacted ascending, with the causal test folded into a per-row
111	   mask over the gathered positions. `attn.attn` 1.024 → **0.454** (2.15x on the
112	   4-layer probe; 0.566 → 0.303 at 48 layers). **The value plane had to become
113	   cell-major first** — a selected run is `ratio` consecutive cells, one
114	   128-byte line, where transposed it was four halves out of sixteen rows. That
115	   costs the block kernel ~7% and decode nothing.
116	3. **The indexer's score on the matrix cores** (`llm_attn_score_wmma.comp`). It
117	   is a GEMM per indexer head with a rectifier: 0.077 → **0.034**. Chunk-invariant
118	   (a matrix product's rows are independent), and *nearer* llama.cpp's selection
119	   than the scalar kernel (9760 vs 9762 of 6 298 621).
120	4. **`checkBufferRange`** — see [[a-benchmark-that-gets-faster]].
121	
122	**The gather is the first kernel here that is not chunk-invariant and cannot be
123	made so.** Its list is the union of a query tile's sixteen rows, so a chunk
124	ending inside the tile gathers a different list and the online softmax folds the
125	same terms in a different order. It is off under `Graph.PinSchedule` with the
126	other reassociating kernels, and the chunk-equality gates pin it (`SetGather`).
127	A prompt prefilled twice at the same ubatch is still bit-identical; only changing
128	the ubatch moves the last places. Gates: `TestAttnGPUGatherSelectsTheSameCells`
129	(exact on the set), `TestAttnGPUGatherIsTheBlockKernel` (4.1e-06 rms against
130	9.9e-04 from llama.cpp), `TestAttnGPUGatherRungsAgree`,
131	`TestAttnGPUGatherIsDispatched`.
132	
133	**The union is the number that prices all of this, and P13's estimate of it was
134	wrong.** `AttnGPU.SelUnion` measures it: at 128 000 cells a 16-row tile reads
135	**15 145** cells where its rows' union is **7 049** and one row selects 2 051.
136	The gather is therefore 2.15x, not the 3.3x P13 projected, and the 3.4x between
137	the union and one row is the floor a 16-row fragment cannot reach.
138	
139	**What the gathered kernel is bound by, by elimination** — four arms, all
140	1.00x-ish, in [[prefill-rates]]: not the matrix cores (doubling their work costs
141	2.7%), not the barriers, not the gather's own traffic (sharing it across two
142	heads buys 4%). It is the LDS round-trip for the fragments and the per-head
143	softmax scaffolding, both linear in the union.
144	
145	**The fast loop is still `-depth ... -layers 4`, 40 seconds an arm** — and it
146	**overstates** `attn.attn` because its one attention layer is denser than the
147	48-layer mean (19.0% live at bm16/bn16 against 11.7%). Ratios reproduce;
148	absolutes do not.
149	
150	    /tmp/pp -model $M -depth -depths 0,64000,128000 -pp 2048 -tg 4 -ctx 136000 -layers 4
151	
152	**Control arms**: `LLM_ATTN_GATHER=0`, `LLM_ATTN_GATHER_KERNEL=qt1_kt1|qt1_kt4`,
153	`LLM_ATTN_GATHER_GRP`, `LLM_ATTN_GATHER_HEADS`, `LLM_ATTN_EXPAND_CELLS=1` (also
154	what `Cells()` needs), `LLM_ATTN_SCORE=scalar`.
155	
156	**The whole-model check.** Three of the four changes claim bit-exactness, and
157	`TestGraphLogits` confirms all three at once: its diagnostics come back
158	byte-identical to the base (`maxAbs 2.507e+00 at 141557`, `rms 5.148e-01`, the
159	same top ten) through all 48 layers. Its *failure* is the pre-existing one — see
160	[[llm-test-suite-gotchas]], and note that a relative `LLM_BANK_CACHE` there
161	writes 23 GB into `llm/models`, which this session walked into.
162	
163	See [[prefill-rates]], [[context-depth-rates]], [[a-benchmark-that-gets-faster]],
164	[[llm-bench-needs-bank-cache]], [[never-edit-source-during-a-sweep]],

166	---
167	name: prefill-rates
168	description: "Prompt-processing rates after P12 (2026-09-21), the ubatch curve and the decode cost that comes with it, what the MoE prefill GEMM is bound by, and the four prefill ideas that are measured dead."
169	metadata: 
170	  node_type: memory
171	  type: project
172	  originSessionId: d77f87a5-b722-4ac5-aaa9-d322f713f1da
173	  modified: 2026-09-21T22:34:23.069Z
174	---
175	
176	**Prefill does not plateau where llama.cpp's does, so the ubatch is a real
177	knob — but widening it is a trade, not a free win.** 48 layers, shipped banks,
178	two runs each (`results/p12_pp_*.csv`, write-ups `research/p11-prefill.md` and
179	`research/p12-prefill-round-two.md`):
180	
181	**Superseded at depth by P14 (2026-09-22)** — see [[long-context-prefill-128k]]
182	for the rates against context depth, which are no longer these. The depth-zero
183	ladder below stands.
184	
185	| ubatch | P11 | P12 | vs llama.cpp |
186	|---:|---:|---:|---:|
187	| 512 | 681.7 | 683.3 | 1.75x |
188	| 2048 | 1191.8 | **1207.7** | 3.08x |
189	| 4096 | 1340.7 | 1363.5 | 3.48x |
190	| 8192 | 1372.2 | **1403.9** | **3.59x** |
191	
192	Against **context depth** at ubatch 2048: 1154.6 / 968.1 / 894.3 / 805.7 /
193	**667.7** tok/s at 0 / 8k / 16k / 32k / 64k. Arms are reproducible to
194	0.1-0.5%, so a 1.2% difference is real; quote means of two passes.
195	
196	**`-llm-batch` defaults to 4096 since P12 — and the wide arenas cost 8% of
197	decode.** This is the thing to remember, because the graph ladder cannot see
198	it (it never decodes). Measured *through the server*, four distinct
199	4.1-4.5k-token prompts, ctx 8192, two interleaved passes agreeing to 0.5%:
200	
201	| batch | prefill | TTFT (4249 tok) | decode |
202	|---:|---:|---:|---:|
203	| 2048 | 1020.9 | 4.33 s | 28.04 |
204	| 4096 | **1146.3** (1.12x) | **3.87 s** | **25.81** (0.92x) |
205	
206	Sixteen non-overlapping samples, at both 8 and 256 generated tokens. A decode
207	step streams 4.1 GB of weights a token and the extra ~1.5 GB of arenas sits in
208	the same memory. **The two rates cross at ~150 generated tokens**: 4096 is
209	1.10x at 8 tokens, 2048 is 1.07x at the 1024 `-llm-max-tokens` defaults to. So
210	4096 ships as the *interactive* default; a batch summariser should set 2048.
211	**Why arenas a decode step never reads cost it 8% is unexplained** and is the
212	open question — if it is layout not volume it may be recoverable.
213	
214	**The MoE prefill GEMM is bound by its per-tile slab unpack, not by rows.**
215	Measured four ways in P11 (row padding 1.90x → 1.19x is worth *nothing*; a
216	per-fragment bound, three sub-lists, and BM 128 all lose). So the way to speed
217	`moe.up` up is fewer tiles at the same block width = fewer experts touched = a
218	bigger ubatch. P12 adds the floor: **gutting the whole Q4_K scale path is only
219	1.21x**, and what remains after the loads are collected — an int→float
220	convert, an FMA and an f16 convert per weight — has **no bit-exact cheaper
221	form** (packed fp16 costs ~13 bits of mantissa; `v_cvt_pkrtz` rounds toward
222	zero). At 21.1 TFLOP/s and 61 GB/s of bank it is neither matrix-core- nor
223	bandwidth-bound.
224	
225	**What is measured dead (do not re-attempt without new information):**
226	
227	- **Four arms on the gathered attention kernel, P14 (2026-09-22)**, and together
228	  they say what it is bound by. *Doubling the QK matrix work costs 2.7%*, so the
229	  matrix cores are ~5% of it. A subgroup staging barrier instead of a workgroup
230	  one is **1.00x**; staging two head-dim groups a barrier is **1.00x** and four
231	  is **0.75x**; putting two query heads in one workgroup so they share the staged
232	  key and value — which halves both the gather's global reads and its LDS writes
233	  — is **1.04x**, and four is **0.75x**. So it is not the matrix cores, not the
234	  barriers, not the gather's traffic and not occupancy-to-spare: what is left is
235	  the **LDS round-trip for the fragments and the per-head softmax scaffolding**,
236	  both of which scale with the union, which is why the kernel's cost is linear in
237	  the cells it visits. The 0.75x arms are LDS crowding out waves.
238	  `LLM_ATTN_GATHER_GRP` and `LLM_ATTN_GATHER_HEADS` are the ladders, both at 1.
239	
240	- **Compacting the live key blocks into a per-query-tile list is 1.00x at
241	  every depth** (P13, 2026-09-22) — it deletes 83% of the axis walk at 128k
242	  and `attn.attn` does not move. Third instance of the same rule, which is now
243	  the engine's and not any kernel's: *latency and redundant reads that matter
244	  at decode do not matter at prefill, because prefill has occupancy* — 3072
245	  single-wave workgroups against a decode step's 24. See
246	  [[long-context-prefill-128k]].
247	
248	- **`hc.cn`'s 256-way reduction tree costs nothing** — deleting it outright is
249	  5331.5 µs against 5325.8. The non-bit-exact subgroup rewrite P11 queued
250	  would have bought zero.
251	- **`hc.cn`'s per-token gamma read costs nothing** — replacing it with a
252	  constant is 5332.9 µs. It is 40 KB and the MALL serves it. Its 57% of copy
253	  bandwidth is now *unexplained and out of hypotheses*.
254	- **Hoisting the attention block skip out of the loop is 1.00x at every
255	  depth.** At 64k a query tile skips ~1480 blocks, each on a dependent global
256	  read; voting on the whole key range up front with a subgroup ballot buys
257	  nothing, because **a prefill dispatches 3072 single-wave workgroups where a
258	  decode step dispatches 24** — latency that matters at decode does not matter
259	  at prefill, because prefill has occupancy. The exact converse of P8. **Still
260	  live for decode**, where it was deliberately never built.
261	- **The selection mask loop is 3.5-8%** of the attention kernel, not the rest
262	  of the depth gap.
263	
264	**At depth the fast loop is `-depth -layers 4`, 40 seconds an arm**
265	([[long-context-prefill-128k]]) — `-attn` runs at `past = 0` and never
266	reaches depth's regime.
267	
268	**`cmd/llm -attn` is the fast loop for attention at depth zero and it is 1.9 seconds** (two
269	layers, real routing, real selection, per-label µs a layer) — use it, not the
270	7-minute `-graph` ladder. It tops out near 16 384 tokens (32 768 in one batch
271	trips P0's watchdog) and runs at `past = 0`, so it reaches the selection's
272	regime but **not depth's**; only `-depth` does. `cmd/llm -moe` is the MoE's
273	equivalent at 228 ms to stage. See [[context-depth-rates]] for decode,
274	[[llm-bench-needs-bank-cache]], [[never-edit-source-during-a-sweep]],
275	[[llm-test-suite-gotchas]].
276	---
277	name: decode-is-latency-not-bandwidth
278	description: "At decode this model's per-head GPU kernels are single waves that all fit on the device at once, so a dispatch costs one wave's serial walk — not its traffic and not its total work."
279	metadata:
280	  type: project
281	---
282	
283	**P8, 2026-09-21.** The probe that settles it: cutting the attention grid from
284	24 workgroups to 2 — a twelfth of the work *and* a twelfth of the traffic —
285	measured **1.00x at every depth** (0, 16 384 and 65 536 cells, three decimal
286	places).
287	
288	The reason is structural and applies well beyond attention. A decode step is
289	**one token**, so any kernel gridded on (query blocks, heads) or on (tokens,
290	…) dispatches a handful of workgroups; `local_size_x = WAVE` makes each one a
291	single wave; and this device has **40 compute units**. Everything launches at
292	once, nothing queues, and the dispatch's wall clock is the *longest single
293	wave's serial loop*. With one wave per CU there is nothing to hide a
294	`coopMatLoad`'s latency behind, which is why the measured rate was ~7 GB/s
295	where prefill on the same kernel achieves hundreds.
296	
297	So at decode:
298	
299	- **Adding parallelism across heads buys nothing** — they already run
300	  concurrently.
301	- **Removing redundant traffic buys nothing** — the redundant readers were
302	  never queued behind each other. (12 query heads share each of the 2 KV
303	  planes here and each re-reads it in full; deleting that is free and worth
304	  nothing.)
305	- **Only shortening the per-workgroup loop helps**, by splitting the reduction
306	  axis across more workgroups, or by making the loop's iterations fewer.
307	
308	Two kernels were fixed this way and a third is open — see
309	[[context-depth-rates]] for the numbers and `research/p8-decode-attention-split.md`.
310	`llm_attn_select.comp` is still one workgroup a token.
311	
312	**How to apply:** before optimising any decode kernel in this repo, check its
313	grid at `rows == 1` first. If it is tens of workgroups, the question is the
314	length of one wave's loop and *not* the bytes it moves — and the cheap probe
315	is to cut the grid and see whether the time moves at all. Do not reason from
316	bandwidth at decode; that reasoning is right at prefill and wrong here.

318	name: strix-halo-bench-runs
319	description: "How the strix-halo-vulkan benchmark suite is run and how long each family takes, plus the run-quality conventions the repo's docs expect."
320	metadata: 
321	  node_type: memory
322	  type: project
323	  originSessionId: 6c27486f-644d-4f43-a0b0-6ebe2136679b
324	  modified: 2026-09-18T12:55:03.680Z
325	---
326	
327	`go run ./cmd/bench -blocks 32,64,128,256,512,1024 <family>` — the non-default
328	block list is what every committed `results/*.csv` was measured with, so keep
329	it if rows are to stay comparable. `go generate ./...` first if any `.comp`
330	changed (`*.spv` is gitignored). As of 2026-09-13 the `moe` family is ~9
331	minutes / 896 rows; it prints its summary tables only at the end, so there is
332	no progress output to poll — run it in the foreground with a long timeout.
333	The `bank` family (added 2026-09-15, research/llm-vertical.md L0a) is the odd one out: its 72
334	timed cells are seconds, but `go run ./cmd/bench -bankgib 64 -bankreadmib 1024
335	bank` first allocates 64 GiB in 19 buffers and writes one word per 4 KB page,
336	which is most of its ~3-minute wall clock. Check `free -g` has the headroom
337	before starting it.
338	
339	**A whole-model tok/s number is only comparable against a control run the
340	same hour** (P1c, 2026-09-18): with an identical binary the decode step
341	measured 30.51 ms one day and 39.20 the next — every *dense-bank* kernel
342	1.6-1.9x slower (dn.qkv 115→206 us, head 1964→3531) while every MoE
343	expert-bank rung was unchanged. Suspected GTT page fragmentation of the
344	float-staged dense banks (32-day uptime, swap 100% full); unprovable without
345	root. **And a difference below ~0.5 tok/s needs interleaved A/B/A/B pairs, not one
346	pair** (P3, 2026-09-18): three pairs of the same two banks gave −0.06, +0.14
347	and +0.05 tok/s, so either single pair would have reported a signed number
348	where the truth was a within-arm spread of 0.31 against a real difference of
349	~0.04. Quote the means and the within-arm spread, not one delta.
350	
351	So when measuring a decode/prefill change, rebuild yesterday's code in
352	a worktree (`.spv` are gitignored — regenerate or copy them) and run both
353	binaries back to back; never quote a delta against a prior day's CSV. Also:
354	run 1 of a freshly staged graph diverges from runs 2+ at ~1.6e-5 in the
355	logits (research/p1c-prerecorded-decode.md finding 4) — warm the graph once
356	before any bitwise comparison.
357	
358	One-token `-ladder` runs of `cmd/llm` (moe/dn/attn/hc) must defeat the 32 MiB
359	MALL or every rate is an L3 number: stage many layers and use `-iters 1`
360	(e.g. `-moe -tokens 1 -ladder -layers 16 -iters 1`, P1b 2026-09-18 —
361	`ProfileSweep` walks a dispatch kind across layers, so each timing reads a
362	cold bank). The screen: any CSV row whose gbps exceeds 242 was not measuring
363	DRAM. The default two-layer, 20-iter form re-reads a ~32 MB working set from
364	the MALL.
365	
366	**`go generate` after a `.comp` edit is load-bearing, and skipping it fails
367	*silently and flatteringly*.** `.spv` is gitignored and embedded into the Go
368	binary, so an edited shader that was not regenerated runs the **previous**
369	kernel — and a hand-compile to `/tmp` to check syntax is not the same thing.
370	On 2026-09-19 (P5b) that produced a whole round of measurements that read as a
371	2x speed-up and a full set of green tests, because the old kernel was doing
372	half the work on the new grid. Regenerate just the families touched
373	(`grep "go:generate" shaders/shaders.go | grep <file>.comp | sed 's|^//go:generate ||'`
374	into a loop) and check the `.spv` mtime before believing any number.
375	
376	**Why:** the repo's TODO.md handoffs report a reproducibility figure for every
377	session (two runs of the family, median ratio and p10-p90 over common rows),
378	so a session that measures anything is expected to run its family twice and
379	quote the agreement.
380	
381	**How to apply:** budget ~20 minutes for two `moe` runs, save each log and CSV
382	to the scratchpad so run N-1 survives for the comparison, and check nothing
383	else is using the GPU (`/sys/class/drm/card1/device/gpu_busy_percent`) before
384	starting. **"Nothing else" includes your own `go build` and `go test`** — a
385	whole-model decode step is ~3 ms of host work in ~28, and compiling beside a
386	`-gen` run cost one control pass 1.6 tok/s of 35 (P4c, 2026-09-19), which is
387	four times the difference such a run is usually measuring. Start the
388	measurement detached (`setsid nohup … &`, or the foreground loop will kill it
389	when the tool call times out) and edit *text* while it runs, nothing else. Do not poll with `pgrep -f` — see
390	[[watch-loops-must-not-match-themselves]].
391	---
392	name: llm-bench-needs-bank-cache
393	description: "Benchmarking cmd/llm on the shipped banks needs LLM_BANK_CACHE set by hand, or every process start re-fits the MoE bank for eight minutes on all 32 cores."
394	metadata:
395	  type: project
396	---
397	
398	**`cmd/serve` sets `LLM_BANK_CACHE`; `cmd/llm` never does** (the comment at
399	`cmd/serve/main.go:177` says so outright). So a `cmd/llm` run launched with
400	`LLM_MOE_BANK` at the shipped plan but no cache path re-fits `ffn_down_exps`
401	to IQ4_NL from scratch: 40 billion weights through a sixteen-scale search,
402	`parallelFor` across every core. Measured 2026-09-19: **31 of 32 cores pinned
403	flat for the whole fit, 5731 CPU-seconds in the first 200 s, sys time 9.3 s**
404	— all arithmetic, no I/O. research/llm-vertical.md D21 prices the whole fit at ~8 minutes.
405	
406	Set it and staging is a disk read instead:
407	
408	    LLM_BANK_CACHE=models/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF/bank-cache
409	
410	With it, a 48-layer stage at 131k cells was **58.5 s total, MoE block 19.4 s**,
411	71.01 GB of weights + 5.09 GB of arenas. The cache directory is 26 GB and was
412	already complete for the shipped plan (48/48 files per family). It is keyed on
413	(tensor, shape, source type, target type, arm, version) and lives inside the
414	checkpoint's directory — it does **not** hash the source bytes.
415	
416	**The dense bank has no cache at all** (`llm/bank_q4.go`), so it re-fits every
417	start no matter what. Measured on the same 16 dense layers: banks off **8.6 s
418	wall / 46.9 CPU-s**, dense bank on **17.4 s / 134.6 CPU-s** — 2.9x the CPU.
419	That part is unavoidable today.
420	
421	**Why:** the CPU storm looks alarming and looks like inference gone wrong — it
422	is neither. It is startup-only weight preparation, which is why the served API
423	never shows it: the server pays the fit once ever and then holds the model
424	resident. During real inference the GPU sits at 98-99% and host cost is ~3 ms
425	of a ~31 ms token.
426	
427	**How to apply:** set `LLM_BANK_CACHE` in every `cmd/llm` invocation that also
428	sets `LLM_MOE_BANK`, and budget ~60 s of staging rather than ~8 minutes. See
429	[[llm-resident-run]] and [[strix-halo-bench-runs]].
430	---
431	name: llm-resident-run
432	description: The whole-model runs (`cmd/llm -resident`, `-graph`, `-gen`, `-ppl`, `cmd/serve -llm`, `TestGraphLogits`) stage 82-83 GB of qwen3.8-flash-next; what they cost in time and RAM, and why nothing else can run beside them.
433	metadata:
434	  type: project
435	---
436	
437	**Since L8a/L8b the dense banks are int8 rather than halves and residency is
438	81.89 GB with the head** (`-dense` 4.32 GB); `LLM_DENSE_FP16=1` puts every
439	block back on the old halves and restores the old sizes exactly, which is how
440	the two are compared. **A decode token is 31.7 ms and residency 79.85 GB as of
441	L8c-7 (2026-09-17)** with all five 4.5-bit families named in
442	`LLM_DENSE_BANK` — 40.5 ms at L8e, 33.3 at L8c-6, ~134 before L7d — so `-n 64`
443	is a ~2.0 s tail on top of staging. Without `LLM_DENSE_BANK` the run is still
444	L8a's int8 bank at 81.89 GB and 40.5 ms.
445	
446	**Do not schedule a whole-model run above ~2560 rows**: at 48 layers
447	`-graph -tokens 3072` (or `-ppl -ctx 4096`) **never returns** — it stalls
448	inside the driver's submit with one host thread at 100% and the GPU at 2-3%,
449	and the shim's 20 s fence timeout never fires, so it hangs indefinitely rather
450	than erroring. 2048 and 2560 are fine; the 4-layer prefix is fine at 4096.
451	This is a known open question in `research/llm-vertical.md`, not a mistake to re-discover.
452	
453	`go run ./cmd/llm -resident` (added 2026-09-16, research/llm-vertical.md L6a) stages every layer
454	of all five blocks: **84.20 GB of device buffers (82.40 since L8a), ~35 s wall
455	clock**, and it
456	ends with about 41 GB of MemAvailable left on this 117.7 GiB machine. Peak
457	host memory is separate — the dense blocks dequantise to f32 before packing,
458	and the 36 DeltaNet layers are 8.35 GB of transient floats at once — which is
459	why the tool stages dense first and the 77 GB expert bank last.
460	
461	**Why:** it is the only thing in the repo that takes most of the machine, so a
462	second GPU or large-allocation job started beside it will either fail to
463	allocate or perturb the timing it prints. `-bank N,N,...` restages just the
464	bank, which is the cheap way to vary residency; `-dense` is the 6.8 GB half
465	and runs in 8 s.
466	
467	`go run ./cmd/llm -graph` and `go test ./llm/ -run TestGraphLogits` (added
468	2026-09-16, research/llm-vertical.md L6b) are the same weight but **85.47 GB**, because they add
469	the 1.27 GB lm head; `-tokens 2048` adds another ~1.1 GB of arenas. Staging is
470	~35-40 s, so budget a 1800 s timeout. Both take a `-layers 4` / `GraphOpts{
471	Layers: 4}` prefix that is 7.4 GB and three seconds — use that while changing
472	anything about the order, and the full stage only for the gate.
473	
474	`go run ./cmd/llm -gen` (added 2026-09-16, research/llm-vertical.md L7c) is the same 85.47 GB
475	plus the KV cache, and it is the slow one: staging is ~35-50 s and generation
476	is **~40.5 ms a token** (see above), so `-n 64` is a ~2.6 s tail on top.
477	**Every committed decode CSV is `-prompt 'The capital of France is'`**; the
478	flag's default is the 81-token `graphDefaultPrompt`, on which the model emits
479	EOS at the first step and the decode row is meaningless. A 900 s timeout
480	covers `-n 64`; a two-minute one does not even cover the staging. `-layers 4`
481	is 7.4 GB, ~2 s to stage and ~18 ms a token, which is the right thing to use
482	for anything about the loop rather than about the rate.
483	
484	`go run ./cmd/llm -ppl` (added 2026-09-17, research/llm-vertical.md L8c-0) is the longest of
485	them: 81.89 GB, ~37 s of staging and then **3.3 s per 2048-token chunk for 145
486	chunks — 7m58s** over `wiki.test.raw`, so run it in the background and wait on
487	the log rather than holding a foreground timeout. `-chunks N` cuts it (4
488	chunks is ~15 s after staging) but **only screens for broken**: four chunks
489	read +0.32% against llama.cpp where the whole corpus reads −0.13%, sign and
490	all. `-layers 4` plus `-chunks 2` is the 8 GB plumbing check. The reference
491	side is `llama-perplexity -c 2048 -b 2048`, ~6.5 s a chunk, and it needs the
492	machine too — never both at once. **`LLM_DENSE_SIM=<plan>` forces the fp16
493	arm** (L8c-1), so a simulated run is the old 84 GB residency and ~6 s longer
494	to stage, and its tok/s means nothing — it grades accuracy only.
495	`LLM_DENSE_SIM_QUANT=imatrix` needs `models/…/imatrix_unsloth.gguf` (the
496	fetch script gets it; note the source's `_file` suffix) and adds ~10 s of
497	staging for the nineteen-rung scale search.
498	
499	**Since P4b/D20 (2026-09-19) a served-default run also stages the MoE bank
500	narrower, and it is not free at startup.** `LLM_MOE_BANK` (default off in
501	`cmd/llm`, set to `llm.ShippedMoEBank` by `cmd/serve -llm`) transcodes four
502	tensor families out of the checkpoint's bytes — 4.2 B weights of
503	`ffn_down_exps` plus 236 M of the shared expert — so **the MoE block stages
504	in ~52 s instead of ~25**, and a whole-model run is ~1m32s to first chunk
505	rather than ~40 s. Residency drops 77.41 -> 76.00 GB in that block (78.53 GB
506	whole-model with D19's dense bank). Budget the extra minute in every timeout;
507	`LLM_MOE_BANK=off` is the control.
508	
509	`go run ./cmd/serve -llm` (added 2026-09-17, research/llm-vertical.md L9a) is the same residency
510	held open: **33.5 s to stage at `-llm-ctx 4096`**, ~84 GB, and it then serves
511	until interrupted. A request is a prefill plus ~44 ms a token (22.7 tok/s
512	through the server on the L8 banks), so a 48-token answer is under a second.
513	Start it in the background, poll the log for `listening on`, and **kill it
514	with `pkill -f '[e]xe/serve'` when finished** — the bracket matters, because
515	`pkill -f 'exe/serve'` matches the shell running it and kills the session
516	instead (the same trap as [[watch-loops-must-not-match-themselves]]). It holds
517	the machine for as long as it runs. `-llm-layers 4` is the 7 GB, 3.5 s prefix
518	and is the right thing for anything about HTTP rather than about the text.
519	
520	**The access log prints no bodies by default** (`-log-bodies` turns them back
521	on): a chat server's bodies are conversations. The per-request `llm:` line is
522	separate and always printed — prompt tokens, how many were reused from the
523	last turn, and the two rates.
524	
525	**The model path must name a shard, not the directory.**
526	`models/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF/` now holds three checkpoints — the model, the
527	imatrix and the MTP head — so `gguf.OpenSet` refuses it as ambiguous and
528	`cmd/llm`'s own `-model` default no longer resolves. Pass
529	`models/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-UD-Q4_K_XL-00001-of-00004.gguf`,
530	which is what `cmd/serve` defaults to.
531	
532	**`-layers 24` is the end-to-end instrument when 48 will not fit.** With the
533	`ai` user service resident (~7 GB) this machine has ~80 GB MemAvailable
534	against a 48-layer `-graph`'s ~80 GB, which is too tight to schedule. A
535	24-layer `-graph` is **~40 GB, ~2 min to first number**, and it is a *real*
536	whole-graph measurement — all five blocks, the head, the host loop, the
537	per-block ms columns in the CSV — not a block bench. Its one distortion is
538	that the M-independent fixed costs (head 2.4 ms, `ple`, `move`, host) are 24%
539	of a step there against 13% at 48 layers, so any *ratio* read off it is
540	optimistic and the 48-layer number is owed (P5, 2026-09-19).
541	
542	**How to apply:** run them in the foreground with a long timeout and nothing
543	else on the GPU, the way [[strix-halo-bench-runs]] asks. `-resident`'s closing
544	measurement (layer 3's MoE block) is comparable to `-moe -tokens 512 -iters 10`
545	only at the same iteration count.

---
name: decode-at-depth-after-p15
description: "Decode rates against context depth after P15 (2026-09-22), the four terms a deep decode step is made of, and the three control knobs — supersedes the P10 table for decode."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: dedbcc64-a855-44f2-a0fa-3d37d0946061
  modified: 2026-09-22T15:25:15.756Z
---

**Quote this table for decode, not P10's and not P14's.** 48 layers, shipped
banks, `-pp 2048 -tg 16 -ctx 139000`, `wiki.test.raw`, write-up
`research/p15-decode-at-depth.md`.

| depth | pp tok/s | tg tok/s | tg ms/tok |
|------:|---------:|---------:|----------:|
| 0 | 1150.7 | 29.73 | 33.6 |
| 8 000 | 969.6 | 28.78 | 34.8 |
| 32 000 | 915.3 | 28.72 | 34.8 |
| 64 000 | 892.8 | 28.14 | 35.5 |
| 128 000 | 829.4 | **27.20** | 36.8 |
| falloff | 0.72x | **0.91x** | |

Decode at 128k was 22.58 before P15 and the falloff 0.76x. **Prefill did not
move** (826.5 → 829.4 at 128k) and is P14's; it was P15's control.

**A deep decode step is four terms and nothing else.** Every other kernel in
the model is flat in depth — `moe.up` 5.44 ms a token at both ends, `dn.qkv`
4.39, `hc.cn` 2.33. At 128 000 cells, base → final:

- `attn.attn.split` 4.109 → **1.571** (the gather+split, P15-3)
- host `gather`, i.e. `PLERows` 5.175 → **1.263** (P15-1)
- `attn.score` 2.533 → **0.995** (the stripe at 64, P15-2)
- `attn.select` 0.862 → **0.862** — untouched, and now the largest
  depth-scaling term left on the device

**The largest one was on the host.** `PLERows(cfg, g.ids)` hashed the whole
sequence every token and sliced off the tail — 8.2 MB allocated and 2.05 M rows
per step at 128k to use sixteen. `PLERowsFrom` is the tail-only form and is
exact by construction. The `-depth` bench had been printing that as a `gather`
line growing 3.1% → 11.7% with depth for as long as it has existed. **Read the
host lines of the profile, not only the kernel ones.**

**The control knobs**, all env, all on `cmd/llm -depth`:

    LLM_ATTN_GATHER=0            # P8's block split, which is what decode had
    LLM_ATTN_GATHER_MIN=<cells>  # the depth the gathered arm turns on at
    LLM_ATTN_CELL_SPLITS=16      # P9's stripe count, shipped at 64
    LLM_ARENA_UNCACHED=1         # the arena memory type
    LLM_NO_PRERECORD=1           # re-record every decode step

**The gates after touching any of this** (plus P7-P10's, in
[[context-depth-rates]]):

    go test ./llm/ -run TestPLERowsFromIsTheTail                   # exact
    go test ./llm/ -run TestAttnGPUGatherSplitIsTheGather          # tolerance
    go test ./llm/ -run TestPrerecordedDecodeCrossesTheGatherBound # the epoch

**Two traps this pass walked into, both worth remembering.** A split-kernel
test that uploads the whole fixture at once passes with 0.000e+00 on every arm,
because `attnSplits` refuses any batch wider than `attnSplitMaxRows` — a split
that never engaged looks exactly like a perfect one, so assert on a zero. And
the obvious test for the prerecord epoch — diff the logits across the bound
with the replay on and off — **cannot fail**, because below the selection's
2051-cell width the gathered and block kernels are bit-identical; assert the
mechanism (`preEpoch` against the depth) instead.

**How to apply:** needs `LLM_BANK_CACHE` — see [[llm-bench-needs-bank-cache]],
[[strix-halo-bench-runs]], [[never-edit-source-during-a-sweep]] and
[[llm-resident-run]]. The fast loop is `-depths 128000 -pp 2048 -tg 8 -layers 4`,
~60 s an arm, and it reproduces the `attn.attn` ratios to the microsecond.
---
name: long-context-prefill-128k
description: "Prefill against depth out to 128k after P14 (2026-09-22): 826 tok/s at ubatch 2048 and 946 at 8192, the four changes, the four measured refusals, and the fast 4-layer probe."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 80f71c47-a621-4724-a77a-e285f8d84b61
  modified: 2026-09-22T11:38:44.739Z
---

**128 000 cells prefills at 826.0 tok/s at ubatch 2048 and 946.1 at
8192 — `GOALS.md`'s 900 is met.** P13 left it at 563.6. 48 layers, shipped banks,
`wiki.test.raw`, one sequence walked forward, `-tg 8 -ctx 139000`. Write-up
`research/p14-prefill-at-depth.md`.

| depth | P13 pp | P14 pp | | decode |
|------:|-------:|-------:|----:|-------:|
| 0 | 1129.3 | 1154.2 | 1.02x | 29.31 |
| 32 000 | 825.8 | 915.6 | 1.11x | 25.80 |
| 64 000 | 719.6 | 892.1 | 1.24x | 24.46 |
| 96 000 | 607.9 | 832.3 | 1.37x | 22.80 |
| **128 000** | **563.6** | **826.0** | **1.47x** | 22.18 |

Falloff from depth zero **0.50x → 0.72x**. Against the ubatch at 128 000 alone
(two runs each): 826.0 at 2048, 886.1 at 4096 (the shipped
`-llm-batch`), **946.1 at 8192** — P12's trade at depth, so 8192 is a
batch summariser's setting. **Decode is the control and did not move.**

**Four changes.**

1. **The selection runs over block scores, not the expanded per-cell tensor**
   (`llm_attn_selblk.comp`). All `ratio` cells of a pooled block carry one score,
   so a weighted select over `nKV/ratio` entries is the same threshold, ties and
   bitmask. `attn.select` 0.281 → **0.020** (13.8x), `attn.expand` deleted, and
   **1.14 GB of arena** freed at ubatch 2048. Bit-identical, gated by
   `TestAttnGPUSelectBlocksIsTheCellSelect` over four chunk schedules.
2. **The attention runs over a per-cell gather** (`llm_attn_gather.comp` +
   `llm_attn_wmma.comp -DGATHER`). Per query tile, the union of its rows'
   selections compacted ascending, with the causal test folded into a per-row
   mask over the gathered positions. `attn.attn` 1.024 → **0.454** (2.15x on the
   4-layer probe; 0.566 → 0.303 at 48 layers). **The value plane had to become
   cell-major first** — a selected run is `ratio` consecutive cells, one
   128-byte line, where transposed it was four halves out of sixteen rows. That
   costs the block kernel ~7% and decode nothing.
3. **The indexer's score on the matrix cores** (`llm_attn_score_wmma.comp`). It
   is a GEMM per indexer head with a rectifier: 0.077 → **0.034**. Chunk-invariant
   (a matrix product's rows are independent), and *nearer* llama.cpp's selection
   than the scalar kernel (9760 vs 9762 of 6 298 621).
4. **`checkBufferRange`** — see [[a-benchmark-that-gets-faster]].

**The gather is the first kernel here that is not chunk-invariant and cannot be
made so.** Its list is the union of a query tile's sixteen rows, so a chunk
ending inside the tile gathers a different list and the online softmax folds the
same terms in a different order. It is off under `Graph.PinSchedule` with the
other reassociating kernels, and the chunk-equality gates pin it (`SetGather`).
A prompt prefilled twice at the same ubatch is still bit-identical; only changing
the ubatch moves the last places. Gates: `TestAttnGPUGatherSelectsTheSameCells`
(exact on the set), `TestAttnGPUGatherIsTheBlockKernel` (4.1e-06 rms against
9.9e-04 from llama.cpp), `TestAttnGPUGatherRungsAgree`,
`TestAttnGPUGatherIsDispatched`.

**The union is the number that prices all of this, and P13's estimate of it was
wrong.** `AttnGPU.SelUnion` measures it: at 128 000 cells a 16-row tile reads
**15 145** cells where its rows' union is **7 049** and one row selects 2 051.
The gather is therefore 2.15x, not the 3.3x P13 projected, and the 3.4x between
the union and one row is the floor a 16-row fragment cannot reach.

**What the gathered kernel is bound by, by elimination** — four arms, all
1.00x-ish, in [[prefill-rates]]: not the matrix cores (doubling their work costs
2.7%), not the barriers, not the gather's own traffic (sharing it across two
heads buys 4%). It is the LDS round-trip for the fragments and the per-head
softmax scaffolding, both linear in the union.

**The fast loop is still `-depth ... -layers 4`, 40 seconds an arm** — and it
**overstates** `attn.attn` because its one attention layer is denser than the
48-layer mean (19.0% live at bm16/bn16 against 11.7%). Ratios reproduce;
absolutes do not.

    /tmp/pp -model $M -depth -depths 0,64000,128000 -pp 2048 -tg 4 -ctx 136000 -layers 4

**Control arms**: `LLM_ATTN_GATHER=0`, `LLM_ATTN_GATHER_KERNEL=qt1_kt1|qt1_kt4`,
`LLM_ATTN_GATHER_GRP`, `LLM_ATTN_GATHER_HEADS`, `LLM_ATTN_EXPAND_CELLS=1` (also
what `Cells()` needs), `LLM_ATTN_SCORE=scalar`.

**The whole-model check.** Three of the four changes claim bit-exactness, and
`TestGraphLogits` confirms all three at once: its diagnostics come back
byte-identical to the base (`maxAbs 2.507e+00 at 141557`, `rms 5.148e-01`, the
same top ten) through all 48 layers. Its *failure* is the pre-existing one — see
[[llm-test-suite-gotchas]], and note that a relative `LLM_BANK_CACHE` there
writes 23 GB into `llm/models`, which this session walked into.

See [[prefill-rates]], [[context-depth-rates]], [[a-benchmark-that-gets-faster]],
[[llm-bench-needs-bank-cache]], [[never-edit-source-during-a-sweep]],
[[strix-halo-bench-runs]], [[graphstats-kinds-aliases]].
---
name: prefill-rates
description: "Prompt-processing rates after P12 (2026-09-21), the ubatch curve and the decode cost that comes with it, what the MoE prefill GEMM is bound by, and the four prefill ideas that are measured dead."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: d77f87a5-b722-4ac5-aaa9-d322f713f1da
  modified: 2026-09-21T22:34:23.069Z
---

**Prefill does not plateau where llama.cpp's does, so the ubatch is a real
knob — but widening it is a trade, not a free win.** 48 layers, shipped banks,
two runs each (`results/p12_pp_*.csv`, write-ups `research/p11-prefill.md` and
`research/p12-prefill-round-two.md`):

**Superseded at depth by P14 (2026-09-22)** — see [[long-context-prefill-128k]]
for the rates against context depth, which are no longer these. The depth-zero
ladder below stands.

| ubatch | P11 | P12 | vs llama.cpp |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 512 | 681.7 | 683.3 | 1.75x |
| 2048 | 1191.8 | **1207.7** | 3.08x |
| 4096 | 1340.7 | 1363.5 | 3.48x |
| 8192 | 1372.2 | **1403.9** | **3.59x** |

Against **context depth** at ubatch 2048: 1154.6 / 968.1 / 894.3 / 805.7 /
**667.7** tok/s at 0 / 8k / 16k / 32k / 64k. Arms are reproducible to
0.1-0.5%, so a 1.2% difference is real; quote means of two passes.

**`-llm-batch` defaults to 4096 since P12 — and the wide arenas cost 8% of
decode.** This is the thing to remember, because the graph ladder cannot see
it (it never decodes). Measured *through the server*, four distinct
4.1-4.5k-token prompts, ctx 8192, two interleaved passes agreeing to 0.5%:

| batch | prefill | TTFT (4249 tok) | decode |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2048 | 1020.9 | 4.33 s | 28.04 |
| 4096 | **1146.3** (1.12x) | **3.87 s** | **25.81** (0.92x) |

Sixteen non-overlapping samples, at both 8 and 256 generated tokens. A decode
step streams 4.1 GB of weights a token and the extra ~1.5 GB of arenas sits in
the same memory. **The two rates cross at ~150 generated tokens**: 4096 is
1.10x at 8 tokens, 2048 is 1.07x at the 1024 `-llm-max-tokens` defaults to. So
4096 ships as the *interactive* default; a batch summariser should set 2048.
**Why arenas a decode step never reads cost it 8% is unexplained** and is the
open question — if it is layout not volume it may be recoverable.

**The MoE prefill GEMM is bound by its per-tile slab unpack, not by rows.**
Measured four ways in P11 (row padding 1.90x → 1.19x is worth *nothing*; a
per-fragment bound, three sub-lists, and BM 128 all lose). So the way to speed
`moe.up` up is fewer tiles at the same block width = fewer experts touched = a
bigger ubatch. P12 adds the floor: **gutting the whole Q4_K scale path is only
1.21x**, and what remains after the loads are collected — an int→float
convert, an FMA and an f16 convert per weight — has **no bit-exact cheaper
form** (packed fp16 costs ~13 bits of mantissa; `v_cvt_pkrtz` rounds toward
zero). At 21.1 TFLOP/s and 61 GB/s of bank it is neither matrix-core- nor
bandwidth-bound.

**What is measured dead (do not re-attempt without new information):**

- **Four arms on the gathered attention kernel, P14 (2026-09-22)**, and together
  they say what it is bound by. *Doubling the QK matrix work costs 2.7%*, so the
  matrix cores are ~5% of it. A subgroup staging barrier instead of a workgroup
  one is **1.00x**; staging two head-dim groups a barrier is **1.00x** and four
  is **0.75x**; putting two query heads in one workgroup so they share the staged
  key and value — which halves both the gather's global reads and its LDS writes
  — is **1.04x**, and four is **0.75x**. So it is not the matrix cores, not the
  barriers, not the gather's traffic and not occupancy-to-spare: what is left is
  the **LDS round-trip for the fragments and the per-head softmax scaffolding**,
  both of which scale with the union, which is why the kernel's cost is linear in
  the cells it visits. The 0.75x arms are LDS crowding out waves.
  `LLM_ATTN_GATHER_GRP` and `LLM_ATTN_GATHER_HEADS` are the ladders, both at 1.

- **Compacting the live key blocks into a per-query-tile list is 1.00x at
  every depth** (P13, 2026-09-22) — it deletes 83% of the axis walk at 128k
  and `attn.attn` does not move. Third instance of the same rule, which is now
  the engine's and not any kernel's: *latency and redundant reads that matter
  at decode do not matter at prefill, because prefill has occupancy* — 3072
  single-wave workgroups against a decode step's 24. See
  [[long-context-prefill-128k]].

- **`hc.cn`'s 256-way reduction tree costs nothing** — deleting it outright is
  5331.5 µs against 5325.8. The non-bit-exact subgroup rewrite P11 queued
  would have bought zero.
- **`hc.cn`'s per-token gamma read costs nothing** — replacing it with a
  constant is 5332.9 µs. It is 40 KB and the MALL serves it. Its 57% of copy
  bandwidth is now *unexplained and out of hypotheses*.
- **Hoisting the attention block skip out of the loop is 1.00x at every
  depth.** At 64k a query tile skips ~1480 blocks, each on a dependent global
  read; voting on the whole key range up front with a subgroup ballot buys
  nothing, because **a prefill dispatches 3072 single-wave workgroups where a
  decode step dispatches 24** — latency that matters at decode does not matter
  at prefill, because prefill has occupancy. The exact converse of P8. **Still
  live for decode**, where it was deliberately never built.
- **The selection mask loop is 3.5-8%** of the attention kernel, not the rest
  of the depth gap.

**At depth the fast loop is `-depth -layers 4`, 40 seconds an arm**
([[long-context-prefill-128k]]) — `-attn` runs at `past = 0` and never
reaches depth's regime.

**`cmd/llm -attn` is the fast loop for attention at depth zero and it is 1.9 seconds** (two
layers, real routing, real selection, per-label µs a layer) — use it, not the
7-minute `-graph` ladder. It tops out near 16 384 tokens (32 768 in one batch
trips P0's watchdog) and runs at `past = 0`, so it reaches the selection's
regime but **not depth's**; only `-depth` does. `cmd/llm -moe` is the MoE's
equivalent at 228 ms to stage. See [[context-depth-rates]] for decode,
[[llm-bench-needs-bank-cache]], [[never-edit-source-during-a-sweep]],
[[llm-test-suite-gotchas]].
---
name: decode-is-latency-not-bandwidth
description: "At decode this model's per-head GPU kernels are single waves that all fit on the device at once, so a dispatch costs one wave's serial walk — not its traffic and not its total work."
metadata:
  type: project
---

**P8, 2026-09-21.** The probe that settles it: cutting the attention grid from
24 workgroups to 2 — a twelfth of the work *and* a twelfth of the traffic —
measured **1.00x at every depth** (0, 16 384 and 65 536 cells, three decimal
places).

The reason is structural and applies well beyond attention. A decode step is
**one token**, so any kernel gridded on (query blocks, heads) or on (tokens,
…) dispatches a handful of workgroups; `local_size_x = WAVE` makes each one a
single wave; and this device has **40 compute units**. Everything launches at
once, nothing queues, and the dispatch's wall clock is the *longest single
wave's serial loop*. With one wave per CU there is nothing to hide a
`coopMatLoad`'s latency behind, which is why the measured rate was ~7 GB/s
where prefill on the same kernel achieves hundreds.

So at decode:

- **Adding parallelism across heads buys nothing** — they already run
  concurrently.
- **Removing redundant traffic buys nothing** — the redundant readers were
  never queued behind each other. (12 query heads share each of the 2 KV
  planes here and each re-reads it in full; deleting that is free and worth
  nothing.)
- **Only shortening the per-workgroup loop helps**, by splitting the reduction
  axis across more workgroups, or by making the loop's iterations fewer.

Two kernels were fixed this way and a third is open — see
[[context-depth-rates]] for the numbers and `research/p8-decode-attention-split.md`.
`llm_attn_select.comp` is still one workgroup a token.

**How to apply:** before optimising any decode kernel in this repo, check its
grid at `rows == 1` first. If it is tens of workgroups, the question is the
length of one wave's loop and *not* the bytes it moves — and the cheap probe
is to cut the grid and see whether the time moves at all. Do not reason from
bandwidth at decode; that reasoning is right at prefill and wrong here.
---
name: strix-halo-bench-runs
description: "How the strix-halo-vulkan benchmark suite is run and how long each family takes, plus the run-quality conventions the repo's docs expect."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 6c27486f-644d-4f43-a0b0-6ebe2136679b
  modified: 2026-09-18T12:55:03.680Z
---

`go run ./cmd/bench -blocks 32,64,128,256,512,1024 <family>` — the non-default
block list is what every committed `results/*.csv` was measured with, so keep
it if rows are to stay comparable. `go generate ./...` first if any `.comp`
changed (`*.spv` is gitignored). As of 2026-09-13 the `moe` family is ~9
minutes / 896 rows; it prints its summary tables only at the end, so there is
no progress output to poll — run it in the foreground with a long timeout.
The `bank` family (added 2026-09-15, research/llm-vertical.md L0a) is the odd one out: its 72
timed cells are seconds, but `go run ./cmd/bench -bankgib 64 -bankreadmib 1024
bank` first allocates 64 GiB in 19 buffers and writes one word per 4 KB page,
which is most of its ~3-minute wall clock. Check `free -g` has the headroom
before starting it.

**A whole-model tok/s number is only comparable against a control run the
same hour** (P1c, 2026-09-18): with an identical binary the decode step
measured 30.51 ms one day and 39.20 the next — every *dense-bank* kernel
1.6-1.9x slower (dn.qkv 115→206 us, head 1964→3531) while every MoE
expert-bank rung was unchanged. Suspected GTT page fragmentation of the
float-staged dense banks (32-day uptime, swap 100% full); unprovable without
root. **And a difference below ~0.5 tok/s needs interleaved A/B/A/B pairs, not one
pair** (P3, 2026-09-18): three pairs of the same two banks gave −0.06, +0.14
and +0.05 tok/s, so either single pair would have reported a signed number
where the truth was a within-arm spread of 0.31 against a real difference of
~0.04. Quote the means and the within-arm spread, not one delta.

So when measuring a decode/prefill change, rebuild yesterday's code in
a worktree (`.spv` are gitignored — regenerate or copy them) and run both
binaries back to back; never quote a delta against a prior day's CSV. Also:
run 1 of a freshly staged graph diverges from runs 2+ at ~1.6e-5 in the
logits (research/p1c-prerecorded-decode.md finding 4) — warm the graph once
before any bitwise comparison.

One-token `-ladder` runs of `cmd/llm` (moe/dn/attn/hc) must defeat the 32 MiB
MALL or every rate is an L3 number: stage many layers and use `-iters 1`
(e.g. `-moe -tokens 1 -ladder -layers 16 -iters 1`, P1b 2026-09-18 —
`ProfileSweep` walks a dispatch kind across layers, so each timing reads a
cold bank). The screen: any CSV row whose gbps exceeds 242 was not measuring
DRAM. The default two-layer, 20-iter form re-reads a ~32 MB working set from
the MALL.

**`go generate` after a `.comp` edit is load-bearing, and skipping it fails
*silently and flatteringly*.** `.spv` is gitignored and embedded into the Go
binary, so an edited shader that was not regenerated runs the **previous**
kernel — and a hand-compile to `/tmp` to check syntax is not the same thing.
On 2026-09-19 (P5b) that produced a whole round of measurements that read as a
2x speed-up and a full set of green tests, because the old kernel was doing
half the work on the new grid. Regenerate just the families touched
(`grep "go:generate" shaders/shaders.go | grep <file>.comp | sed 's|^//go:generate ||'`
into a loop) and check the `.spv` mtime before believing any number.

**Why:** the repo's TODO.md handoffs report a reproducibility figure for every
session (two runs of the family, median ratio and p10-p90 over common rows),
so a session that measures anything is expected to run its family twice and
quote the agreement.

**How to apply:** budget ~20 minutes for two `moe` runs, save each log and CSV
to the scratchpad so run N-1 survives for the comparison, and check nothing
else is using the GPU (`/sys/class/drm/card1/device/gpu_busy_percent`) before
starting. **"Nothing else" includes your own `go build` and `go test`** — a
whole-model decode step is ~3 ms of host work in ~28, and compiling beside a
`-gen` run cost one control pass 1.6 tok/s of 35 (P4c, 2026-09-19), which is
four times the difference such a run is usually measuring. Start the
measurement detached (`setsid nohup … &`, or the foreground loop will kill it
when the tool call times out) and edit *text* while it runs, nothing else. Do not poll with `pgrep -f` — see
[[watch-loops-must-not-match-themselves]].
---
name: llm-bench-needs-bank-cache
description: "Benchmarking cmd/llm on the shipped banks needs LLM_BANK_CACHE set by hand, or every process start re-fits the MoE bank for eight minutes on all 32 cores."
metadata:
  type: project
---

**`cmd/serve` sets `LLM_BANK_CACHE`; `cmd/llm` never does** (the comment at
`cmd/serve/main.go:177` says so outright). So a `cmd/llm` run launched with
`LLM_MOE_BANK` at the shipped plan but no cache path re-fits `ffn_down_exps`
to IQ4_NL from scratch: 40 billion weights through a sixteen-scale search,
`parallelFor` across every core. Measured 2026-09-19: **31 of 32 cores pinned
flat for the whole fit, 5731 CPU-seconds in the first 200 s, sys time 9.3 s**
— all arithmetic, no I/O. research/llm-vertical.md D21 prices the whole fit at ~8 minutes.

Set it and staging is a disk read instead:

    LLM_BANK_CACHE=models/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF/bank-cache

With it, a 48-layer stage at 131k cells was **58.5 s total, MoE block 19.4 s**,
71.01 GB of weights + 5.09 GB of arenas. The cache directory is 26 GB and was
already complete for the shipped plan (48/48 files per family). It is keyed on
(tensor, shape, source type, target type, arm, version) and lives inside the
checkpoint's directory — it does **not** hash the source bytes.

**The dense bank has no cache at all** (`llm/bank_q4.go`), so it re-fits every
start no matter what. Measured on the same 16 dense layers: banks off **8.6 s
wall / 46.9 CPU-s**, dense bank on **17.4 s / 134.6 CPU-s** — 2.9x the CPU.
That part is unavoidable today.

**Why:** the CPU storm looks alarming and looks like inference gone wrong — it
is neither. It is startup-only weight preparation, which is why the served API
never shows it: the server pays the fit once ever and then holds the model
resident. During real inference the GPU sits at 98-99% and host cost is ~3 ms
of a ~31 ms token.

**How to apply:** set `LLM_BANK_CACHE` in every `cmd/llm` invocation that also
sets `LLM_MOE_BANK`, and budget ~60 s of staging rather than ~8 minutes. See
[[llm-resident-run]] and [[strix-halo-bench-runs]].

name: llm-resident-run
description: The whole-model runs (`cmd/llm -resident`, `-graph`, `-gen`, `-ppl`, `cmd/serve -llm`, `TestGraphLogits`) stage 82-83 GB of qwen3.8-flash-next; what they cost in time and RAM, and why nothing else can run beside them.
metadata:
  type: project
---

**Since L8a/L8b the dense banks are int8 rather than halves and residency is
81.89 GB with the head** (`-dense` 4.32 GB); `LLM_DENSE_FP16=1` puts every
block back on the old halves and restores the old sizes exactly, which is how
the two are compared. **A decode token is 31.7 ms and residency 79.85 GB as of
L8c-7 (2026-09-17)** with all five 4.5-bit families named in
`LLM_DENSE_BANK` — 40.5 ms at L8e, 33.3 at L8c-6, ~134 before L7d — so `-n 64`
is a ~2.0 s tail on top of staging. Without `LLM_DENSE_BANK` the run is still
L8a's int8 bank at 81.89 GB and 40.5 ms.

**Do not schedule a whole-model run above ~2560 rows**: at 48 layers
`-graph -tokens 3072` (or `-ppl -ctx 4096`) **never returns** — it stalls
inside the driver's submit with one host thread at 100% and the GPU at 2-3%,
and the shim's 20 s fence timeout never fires, so it hangs indefinitely rather
than erroring. 2048 and 2560 are fine; the 4-layer prefix is fine at 4096.
This is a known open question in `research/llm-vertical.md`, not a mistake to re-discover.

`go run ./cmd/llm -resident` (added 2026-09-16, research/llm-vertical.md L6a) stages every layer
of all five blocks: **84.20 GB of device buffers (82.40 since L8a), ~35 s wall
clock**, and it
ends with about 41 GB of MemAvailable left on this 117.7 GiB machine. Peak
host memory is separate — the dense blocks dequantise to f32 before packing,
and the 36 DeltaNet layers are 8.35 GB of transient floats at once — which is
why the tool stages dense first and the 77 GB expert bank last.

**Why:** it is the only thing in the repo that takes most of the machine, so a
second GPU or large-allocation job started beside it will either fail to
allocate or perturb the timing it prints. `-bank N,N,...` restages just the
bank, which is the cheap way to vary residency; `-dense` is the 6.8 GB half
and runs in 8 s.

`go run ./cmd/llm -graph` and `go test ./llm/ -run TestGraphLogits` (added
2026-09-16, research/llm-vertical.md L6b) are the same weight but **85.47 GB**, because they add
the 1.27 GB lm head; `-tokens 2048` adds another ~1.1 GB of arenas. Staging is
~35-40 s, so budget a 1800 s timeout. Both take a `-layers 4` / `GraphOpts{
Layers: 4}` prefix that is 7.4 GB and three seconds — use that while changing
anything about the order, and the full stage only for the gate.

`go run ./cmd/llm -gen` (added 2026-09-16, research/llm-vertical.md L7c) is the same 85.47 GB
plus the KV cache, and it is the slow one: staging is ~35-50 s and generation
is **~40.5 ms a token** (see above), so `-n 64` is a ~2.6 s tail on top.
**Every committed decode CSV is `-prompt 'The capital of France is'`**; the
flag's default is the 81-token `graphDefaultPrompt`, on which the model emits
EOS at the first step and the decode row is meaningless. A 900 s timeout
covers `-n 64`; a two-minute one does not even cover the staging. `-layers 4`
is 7.4 GB, ~2 s to stage and ~18 ms a token, which is the right thing to use
for anything about the loop rather than about the rate.

`go run ./cmd/llm -ppl` (added 2026-09-17, research/llm-vertical.md L8c-0) is the longest of
them: 81.89 GB, ~37 s of staging and then **3.3 s per 2048-token chunk for 145
chunks — 7m58s** over `wiki.test.raw`, so run it in the background and wait on
the log rather than holding a foreground timeout. `-chunks N` cuts it (4
chunks is ~15 s after staging) but **only screens for broken**: four chunks
read +0.32% against llama.cpp where the whole corpus reads −0.13%, sign and
all. `-layers 4` plus `-chunks 2` is the 8 GB plumbing check. The reference
side is `llama-perplexity -c 2048 -b 2048`, ~6.5 s a chunk, and it needs the
machine too — never both at once. **`LLM_DENSE_SIM=<plan>` forces the fp16
arm** (L8c-1), so a simulated run is the old 84 GB residency and ~6 s longer
to stage, and its tok/s means nothing — it grades accuracy only.
`LLM_DENSE_SIM_QUANT=imatrix` needs `models/…/imatrix_unsloth.gguf` (the
fetch script gets it; note the source's `_file` suffix) and adds ~10 s of
staging for the nineteen-rung scale search.

**Since P4b/D20 (2026-09-19) a served-default run also stages the MoE bank
narrower, and it is not free at startup.** `LLM_MOE_BANK` (default off in
`cmd/llm`, set to `llm.ShippedMoEBank` by `cmd/serve -llm`) transcodes four
tensor families out of the checkpoint's bytes — 4.2 B weights of
`ffn_down_exps` plus 236 M of the shared expert — so **the MoE block stages
in ~52 s instead of ~25**, and a whole-model run is ~1m32s to first chunk
rather than ~40 s. Residency drops 77.41 -> 76.00 GB in that block (78.53 GB
whole-model with D19's dense bank). Budget the extra minute in every timeout;
`LLM_MOE_BANK=off` is the control.

`go run ./cmd/serve -llm` (added 2026-09-17, research/llm-vertical.md L9a) is the same residency
held open: **33.5 s to stage at `-llm-ctx 4096`**, ~84 GB, and it then serves
until interrupted. A request is a prefill plus ~44 ms a token (22.7 tok/s
through the server on the L8 banks), so a 48-token answer is under a second.
Start it in the background, poll the log for `listening on`, and **kill it
with `pkill -f '[e]xe/serve'` when finished** — the bracket matters, because
`pkill -f 'exe/serve'` matches the shell running it and kills the session
instead (the same trap as [[watch-loops-must-not-match-themselves]]). It holds
the machine for as long as it runs. `-llm-layers 4` is the 7 GB, 3.5 s prefix
and is the right thing for anything about HTTP rather than about the text.

**The access log prints no bodies by default** (`-log-bodies` turns them back
on): a chat server's bodies are conversations. The per-request `llm:` line is
separate and always printed — prompt tokens, how many were reused from the
last turn, and the two rates.

**The model path must name a shard, not the directory.**
`models/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF/` now holds three checkpoints — the model, the
imatrix and the MTP head — so `gguf.OpenSet` refuses it as ambiguous and
`cmd/llm`'s own `-model` default no longer resolves. Pass
`models/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-UD-Q4_K_XL-00001-of-00004.gguf`,
which is what `cmd/serve` defaults to.

**`-layers 24` is the end-to-end instrument when 48 will not fit.** With the
`ai` user service resident (~7 GB) this machine has ~80 GB MemAvailable
against a 48-layer `-graph`'s ~80 GB, which is too tight to schedule. A
24-layer `-graph` is **~40 GB, ~2 min to first number**, and it is a *real*
whole-graph measurement — all five blocks, the head, the host loop, the
per-block ms columns in the CSV — not a block bench. Its one distortion is
that the M-independent fixed costs (head 2.4 ms, `ple`, `move`, host) are 24%
of a step there against 13% at 48 layers, so any *ratio* read off it is
optimistic and the 48-layer number is owed (P5, 2026-09-19).

**How to apply:** run them in the foreground with a long timeout and nothing
else on the GPU, the way [[strix-halo-bench-runs]] asks. `-resident`'s closing
measurement (layer 3's MoE block) is comparable to `-moe -tokens 512 -iters 10`
only at the same iteration count.
