It is still live for decode, where it was deliberately never built. **The selection mask loop is 3.5-8%**, not the rest of the gap. **The MoE's per-element affine is a floor**: gutting the whole scale path is 1.21x at 2048 tokens, P12-2 takes the loads and integer ops out of that, and what remains — an int→float convert, an FMA and an f16 convert on every weight — has no bit-exact cheaper form, since packed fp16 costs thirteen bits of mantissa and `v_cvt_pkrtz` rounds the wrong way. **The ubatch remains the largest number on the board**: 2048 → 8192 is 1.16x and the curve has not flattened, which is a memory budget rather than a kernel. |

| [P11](p11-prefill.md) | **Prompt processing: the ubatch was the largest number in the file and the cheapest, and the MoE's row padding is not a cost at all.** `cmd/serve` prefilled in **512-token chunks** because that is llama.cpp's best ubatch and what every number in this vertical is quoted against — and 512 is the **worst rung this graph has**. llama.cpp plateaus at its ubatch; this one does not, because the MoE's arithmetic intensity is the **routing's**: at 512 tokens 274 of 512 experts are unpacked whole to serve 5120 rows, and the schedule pads those out to 11 904. `-llm-batch` is now **2048** — 1.12 GB of arenas for **1.64x** (667.4 → 1093.3 tok/s at 48 layers and ctx 4096; **667 → 1053 through HTTP** on a 4128-token prompt), where the 1.49 GB to 4096 buys 13% more. Separately, `llm_moe_gemm.comp`'s MODE 0 stages BM **scattered** rows of the block input into LDS per K-step, and it was doing it one half at a time: **32 two-byte loads a lane a K-step at BM 64**, against the eight the B unpack issues for four times the data. That is L5b-7's finding on the *operand* instead of the weight — the kernel is bound by how many load instructions it issues — so the halves arena is bound a second time as `uvec4` (binding 7) and a row is four aligned loads: **`moe.up` 14 918 → 11 936 µs a layer at 2048 tokens (1.25x)**, bit for bit the same slab, MODE 1 untouched as the control. The graph: **1079.6 → 1165.1 tok/s at 2048 rows, 1250.1 → 1328.5 at 8192 (3.40x llama.cpp)**, two runs agreeing to 0.2%. **Three changes that look right and are not**, all reverted, all one answer: a 16-row alignment with a row count per record (13.7 ms against 11.9 — the per-fragment branch inside the unrolled accumulator loops costs more than 35% of the rows, and the kernel goes to 256 VGPRs), three sub-lists one dispatch a rung (12.5 — no guard anywhere, but small grids do not fill the machine and three grids have three ramps), and a **128-row block** (13.5 — 608 tiles to 477 but the padding to 2.98x, because with 399 experts touched **the floor is one tile an expert** however wide the block). **At prefill this GEMM is bound by its per-tile slab unpack and the rows are very nearly free**; L5b built the padding as a cost to justify and it is not one, so the way in is fewer *tiles*, which is a bigger ubatch — which is the result. **A second round takes it to 3.51x.** `hc.cn` — the combine fused with the next mixer's norm, the second largest kernel in a prefill and one that does **no arithmetic** — was one workgroup per (token, stream), and the four streams of a token combine *the same* block output row: 110 KB a token where 80 would do. One workgroup a token, the output held in ten registers a thread already had spare, is **1.37-1.44x on the kernel** and bit-identical (each stream still reduces through the same 256-way tree), taking the graph to **1191.8 / 1372.2 tok/s** at 2048 / 8192 rows and 64k prefill to **654 tok/s** from 440. 8	- [Deployment is two machines](deployment-two-machines.md) — LLM alone on one, the rest on the other; no footprint quantisation for the small verticals.

10	- [The ai server is a user systemd unit](ai-service-user-unit.md) — `journalctl --user -u ai`, deploy.sh installs it, ~25 s to come up; omitting `-token` does NOT disable auth, and it is served open on purpose.
11	- [Running the MTP draft head](mtp-draft-head-run.md) — `cmd/llm -mtp` is ~80 GB, and `-mtp-free` degenerates into a loop that reads as +18 points of acceptance.
12	- [Running the speculative loop](spec-loop-run.md) — `cmd/llm -spec` is parked at 0.95x; set the shipped banks or you measure the wrong model.
13	- [A new row count needs a graph gate](two-row-regime-needs-a-graph-gate.md) — block tests passed while a two-token pass was 45x wrong.
14	- [Benchmarks need LLM_BANK_CACHE](llm-bench-needs-bank-cache.md) — `cmd/llm` never sets it, so a shipped-bank run re-fits for 8 minutes on 32 cores.
15	- [Prefill out to 128k](long-context-prefill-128k.md) — the gather takes it to 826 tok/s at ubatch 2048 and 946 at 8192; the four changes and the four refusals.
16	- [Decode at depth (P15, P16)](decode-at-depth-after-p15.md) — the table that stands for decode: 34.4 tok/s at depth zero, 31.5 at 128k; the wide-batch cost was a padding bug found by a per-label diff.
17	- [The arena's memory type is free](vulkan-arena-memory-type-is-free.md) — HOST_CACHED costs the GPU nothing at 3.85 GB; stop suspecting it.
18	- [Rates against context depth](context-depth-rates.md) — P7+P8+P9+P10 closed it: 64k decode 4.05 → 27.69 tok/s, falloff 0.14x → 0.79x; the five gates and the control env vars.

21	- [Decode is latency, not bandwidth](decode-is-latency-not-bandwidth.md) — 24 single-wave workgroups all fit at once, so only the length of one wave's loop matters.
22	- [Never edit source during a sweep](never-edit-source-during-a-sweep.md) — `go run` rebuilds per arm; build once to the scratchpad and select arms with env vars.
23	- [GraphStats.Kinds aliases the live graph](graphstats-kinds-aliases.md) — a kept snapshot keeps absorbing dispatches; only the last depth of a sweep was ever right.
24	- [Prefill rates and what bounds them](prefill-rates.md) — the ubatch curve, why a wider `-llm-batch` now costs only memory (P16), and four prefill ideas that are measured dead.

26	- [Three ways the llm test suite misleads](llm-test-suite-gotchas.md) — a 10-minute timeout, a TestGraphLogits failure that is not yours, and 23 GB in llm/models.

attachment.snippet:
1	# P16 — the wide batch never cost decode anything: two moves padded to the arena
2	
3	**2026-09-22.** Three changes, all exact, and two measured refusals. Decode
4	goes **1.16x at every depth** at ubatch 2048 — **29.73 → 34.4 tok/s at depth
5	zero and 27.20 → 31.5 at 128 000 cells** — and the cost of a wide prefill
6	batch on decode, which P12-7 priced at 8% and P15 at 11-22% and nobody could
7	explain, **was a bug and is gone**: at an 8192-row arena decode goes **23.55 →
8	33.87 tok/s (1.44x)**. Prefill is flat as the control.
9	
10	| depth | P15 pp | P16 pp | P15 tg | P16 tg | |
11	|------:|-------:|-------:|-------:|-------:|---:|
12	| 0 | 1150.7 | 1155.8 | 29.73 | **34.39** | 1.16x |
13	| 8 000 | 969.6 | 973.9 | 28.78 | **33.54** | 1.17x |
14	| 32 000 | 915.3 | 919.7 | 28.72 | **33.20** | 1.16x |
15	| 64 000 | 892.8 | 896.3 | 28.14 | **32.41** | 1.15x |
16	| 128 000 | 829.4 | 834.4 | 27.20 | **31.53** | 1.16x |
17	| falloff | 0.72x | 0.72x | 0.91x | 0.92x | |
18	
19	48 layers, shipped banks, `-pp 2048 -tg 16 -ctx 139000`, `wiki.test.raw`.
20	Two passes of the P16 arm, agreeing to 0.2% on tg and 0.4% on pp; the table
21	is their mean. The P15 columns are P15's own table, not a same-hour control —
22	the same-hour controls are the arm tables below, which are.
23	
24	## P16-1: the arena width, and the probe that settled it
25	
26	P15 left the question narrowed to one probe: *stage the wide arenas and
27	prefill in narrow chunks anyway, and see whether the cost follows the arena's
28	width or the prefill's footprint.* `cmd/llm -depth` now takes `-ubatch`, the
29	arena rows, separately from `-pp`, so that is one flag. Depth zero, `-ctx
30	16384`, `-tg 64`, two interleaved passes:
31	
32	| arenas | prefill batch | tg tok/s |
33	|---:|---:|---:|
34	| 2048 | 2048 | 30.17 / 30.59 |
35	| 8192 | **2048** | 23.97 / 24.16 |
36	| 8192 | 8192 | 23.52 / 23.57 |
37	
38	**It follows the arena.** A wide arena that a narrow prefill never filled
39	costs decode the same 21% as one a wide prefill did. And P15 had already shown
40	it is not *volume* — 3.85 GB of extra `-ctx` costs 0.2% — so it had to be
41	something a decode step *does* in proportion to the arena's rows. The per-label
42	diff finds it in one line: everything is flat except three labels.
43	
44	| label | 2048 arena | 8192 arena | Δ ms a token |
45	|---|---:|---:|---:|
46	| `dn.qkv` | 120.3 µs | 233.1 µs | +4.06 |
47	| `move` | 5.5 µs | 19.7 µs | +2.78 |
48	| `attn.qkv` | 128.0 µs | 247.1 µs | +1.43 |
49	| everything else | | | +0.3 |
50	
51	`DeltaNetGPU.InPort` and `AttnGPU.InPort` advertised `Rows: g.arenaRows`, and
52	`mover.Move` writes zeros from the run's rows up to the destination's. So
53	**every decode step zero-filled the whole prefill arena of both blocks' A
54	operand, once a layer** — at 8192 rows, 8192 × 2560 halves = 42 MB a move, 48
55	moves a token. The arithmetic closes: the 48 padded moves are ~63 µs each
56	(the other 148 moves stay at 5.5), which is too fast to have written 42 MB, and
57	the qkv projection that runs next is ~114 µs slower — together ~177 µs a layer,
58	**237 GB/s for 42 MB, which is this device's copy rate**. The move's writes are
59	posted, and the next kernel pays for them draining. The
60	comment on the port said why it was the arena: *the GEMM rungs have no bounds
61	check*. That is true and it asks for `roundUp(rows, bm)`, not the arena — the
62	widest row block any rung reads is what the arena is itself rounded to, so the
63	port now pads to `roundUpInt(g.rows, g.rowAlign)`, which is what the MoE's port
64	(`roundUpInt(g.rows, moeBMMax)`) had done all along.
65	
66	It is not only the wide arenas' bug. At 2048 rows it was 4 MB a move and
67	**9% of decode** (30.38 → 33.13 tok/s with only this change, the `hc.cn`
68	control arm below), and the P12-7 server measurement that made 4096 a trade
69	was this line and nothing else.
70	
71	The mechanism is asserted by `TestInPortPadsTheRunNotTheArena` — one row pads
72	to one row block, a full batch to the arena — because no tolerance can see
73	it: the old padding is *correct*. `TestGraphIsAChunkSplit`,
74	`TestPrerecordedDecodeIsTheRecordedDecode` and 96 greedy tokens on a
75	597-token prompt, identical across the two binaries, hold the answer. And all three
76	changes together are **bit-exact through the whole model**: `TestGraphLogits`
77	at 48 layers prints the same per-depth rms, `result_norm`, logits and top ten
78	to the last digit as the HEAD binary run beside it.
79	
80	## P16-2: `hc.cn` goes back to a stream a workgroup at decode
81	
82	P11 made `hc.cn` one workgroup a **token** instead of one a (token, stream),
83	because the four streams read the same block output row and at prefill the
84	kernel is short of bandwidth: 1.37-1.44x there. At decode it is the P8 rule
85	the other way round: one token is **one workgroup on a forty-CU device**,
86	walking four streams, each through the 256-way tree, in series — **25.0 µs a
87	dispatch, 94 a token, 2.35 ms of a 33.1 ms step**. P1a had priced the fused
88	kernel at ~6-8 µs at one token, and that was before P11.
89	
90	So the grid is chosen by the width: at `rows <= 64` (`hcCNSplitRows`,
91	`LLM_HC_CN_SPLIT_ROWS`, 0 is P11's grid everywhere) it is `(rows, hc)` and a
92	workgroup walks only its own stream. Every stream still reduces the same
93	per-thread partials through the same tree, so the two grids are the same bits;
94	`TestHCFusionIsTheCombineThenTheNorm` now asserts the pair against both.
95	
96	**25.0 → 7.0 µs a dispatch, 33.13 → 35.14 tok/s (1.06x)** at depth zero, two
97	passes each (33.19/33.07 against 35.16/35.12). Prefill is P11's grid and flat.
98	
99	## P16-3: `attn.select`'s emit walks blocks, not cells
100	
101	TODO named `attn.select` the last unstriped decode kernel. Two guesses about
102	what bounds it were measured and are wrong (below); a probe then said where
103	its 68 µs at 128 000 cells go: dropping the emit leaves **43**, and dropping
104	three of the four radix passes also leaves **43** — so ~8 µs a pass, **~25 µs
105	of emit**, and ~10 fixed.
106	
107	The emit walked 32 cells a lane, dividing by the runtime `ratio` a cell and
108	fetching each block's key behind a branch on the last. A block's `ratio` cells
109	all carry its key, so the walk is now a block at a time — one compare and a
110	run of bits — with `EMIT_BATCH` keys fetched before any is compared, and the
111	incomplete tail block handled as its own span. Same bits by construction;
112	`TestAttnGPUSelectBlocksIsTheCellSelect`, `TestAttnGPUSelectionIsTheCPUs`,
113	`TestAttnGPUGatherSelectsTheSameCells` and
114	`TestAttnGPUCacheSizeDoesNotChangeTheAnswer` all pass.
115	
116	**68.1 → 54.9 µs at decode (1.24x) and 3459 → 2876 µs a prefill dispatch
117	(1.20x)** at 128 000 cells, two passes each on the 4-layer probe. It is ~0.4%
118	of a deep token either way — worth having because it is free, and not worth
119	more work: what is left is four ~8 µs passes that are a reduction.
120	
121	## The refusals
122	
123	- **Batching the histogram's loads is 0.96x** (67.0 → 69.6 µs). Four keys in
124	  flight a lane before the first atomic: the pass is not a chain of load
125	  latencies.
126	- **Folding same-bucket lanes a wave before the atomic is 0.69x** (68 →
127	  98 µs). The first pass buckets on sign and exponent, so it looked like ~1024
128	  lanes queuing on two or three LDS words; if they do, it costs less than a
129	  `subgroupMin` + `subgroupAdd` round a trip does.
130	
131	## What changes for the server: `-llm-batch` is no longer a trade
132	
133	P12-7's method repeated: `cmd/serve -llm -llm-ctx 8192`, four disjoint
134	wikitext prompts of 3918-4346 tokens, 256 generated tokens each, greedy, a
135	fresh server per arm, two interleaved passes. The passes agree to 0.1%.
136	
137	| `-llm-batch` | prefill | P12-7 | decode | P12-7 |
138	|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
139	| 2048 | 1052.2 | 1020.9 | **34.19** | 28.04 |
140	| 4096 | 1198.5 | 1146.3 | **34.20** | 25.81 |

aiTitle: LLM prompt processing and token generation speeds

content.text:
I found and fixed a bug that had been slowing every decode step. Decode is now **1.16x faster at every context depth**, and **1.33x faster through the server** at the default batch size of 4096. Prompt processing is unchanged, and all three changes produce exactly the same output as before.

**The results (48 layers, shipped banks):**

| | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| Decode, empty context | 29.73 tok/s | **34.4** |
| Decode, 128k context | 27.20 | **31.5** |
| Decode through the server at `-llm-batch` 4096 | 25.8 | **34.2** |
| Decode with 8192-row prefill buffers | 23.6 | **33.9** |
| Prompt processing at 128k (batch 2048 / 4096) | 829 / 886 | 834 / 905 |

**1. The bug (most of the gain).** Earlier work measured that a wider prompt batch cost decode 8–22% and put it down to memory pressure. That was wrong. Before the DeltaNet and attention layers, each decode step writes the current token into that layer's input buffer and fills the unused rows with zeros. It filled the buffer's full capacity (up to 8,192 rows) instead of just the 64 or 128 rows the kernels actually read. That was up to 42 MB of zeros per layer, twice a layer, on every token.
- I found it by giving the depth benchmark a new `-ubatch` flag, so buffer size and prompt batch can vary separately. The slowdown followed the buffer size, and a per-kernel comparison put all of it on three kernels.
- The fix is two lines, matching what the MoE layer already did.
- It also cost 9% of decode at the smaller 2048 batch. The "4096 speeds up prompts but slows decode" trade-off recorded earlier was entirely this bug.

**2. `hc.cn` at decode (+6%).** An earlier prefill optimisation made this kernel run as one workgroup per token. During decode that meant a single workgroup on a 40-CU GPU working through four streams one after another. At 64 rows or fewer it now runs one workgroup per stream: 25 µs → 7 µs per call.

**3. `attn.select`'s final stage (68 → 55 µs at 128k).** It now works a block of cells at a time instead of cell by cell. This is a small gain.

**Correctness:**
- The full `llm` suite passes: 182 tests, none skipped.
- `TestGraphLogits` at 48 layers gives byte-identical output to the unchanged code run beside it.
- 96 generated tokens are identical between the old and new binaries.
- A new test, `TestInPortPadsTheRunNotTheArena`, fails on the old padding. The old code gave correct answers, just slowly, so no accuracy check could have caught it.

**Measured and dropped:** two other attempts to speed up `attn.select` made it slower (0.96x and 0.69x). Both are reverted and written up.

**Default batch size:** through the server, decode is 34.2 tok/s at 2048, 4096 and 8192 alike, so a wider batch now costs only memory. I kept the default at 4096. Moving to 8192 speeds up only prompts longer than 4,096 tokens (946 vs 886 tok/s at 128k). It holds about 3 GB more memory and lowers the maximum context length, so that's your call for the deployment. I rewrote the advice in `API.md`, `backend/llm.go` and the `-llm-batch` flag help, which all still said to use 2048 for long outputs.

**What's left for decode** is smaller wins of 1–2% each. The biggest is removing the 196 small copy dispatches between layers per token, which means merging the per-block memory buffers into one (a larger refactor).

The write-up is `research/p16-decode-arena-width.md`, and `TODO.md` and `research/README.md` are updated. P15 was never added to the research index, and I left that for its owner. I haven't committed anything; the auto-committer will pick the changes up.
